tests.name: test_products_schema_and_types
tests.doc:
What: GET /products returns a list of {id:int, name:str, price:"0.00" string, stock:int>=0}.
    Why: clients parse these fields; a wrong type or money format breaks checkout and reporting.
    Severity: Medium if broken
    Repro: curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8000/products

tests.name: test_order_schema_and_types
tests.doc:
What: GET /orders/1 as owner returns the documented order shape with money as 2-decimal strings.
    Why: schema drift silently breaks clients and finance exports.
    Severity: Medium if broken
    Repro: curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer alice-token' http://127.0.0.1:8000/orders/1

tests.name: test_order_total_without_coupon
tests.doc:
What: POST /orders 2 x mouse (19.99) with no coupon must total exactly 39.98 (control case).
    Why: proves the pricing bug (if any) is in the discount path, not basic arithmetic.
    Severity: High if broken
    Repro: curl -s -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer alice-token' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"items":[{"product_id":3,"quantity":2}]}' http://127.0.0.1:8000/orders

tests.name: test_order_quantity_boundaries_rejected[-1]
tests.doc:
What: POST /orders with quantity outside 1..100 (negative, zero, 101, 2^31) must be rejected with 422.
    Why: negative quantities create negative totals (refund fraud); huge ones overflow stock and totals.
    Severity: High if broken
    Repro: curl -s -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer alice-token' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"items":[{"product_id":1,"quantity":-1}]}' http://127.0.0.1:8000/orders

exchanges.body: {"detail":[{"type":"greater_than_equal","loc":["body","items",0,"quantity"],"msg":"Input should be greater than or equal to 1","input":-1,"ctx":{"ge":1}}]}

tests.name: test_page_size_boundaries[1-200]
tests.doc:
What: GET /products?limit=N accepts 1..100 and rejects 0, 101 and 1,000,000 with 422.
    Why: an unbounded page size lets one request dump the table and exhaust memory (API4:2023).
    Severity: Medium if broken
    Repro: curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/products?limit=1000000'

tests.name: test_unknown_product_and_coupon
tests.doc:
What: POST /orders with a missing product id -> 404; with an unknown coupon -> 400.
    Why: silent acceptance of bad input creates orders that cannot be fulfilled or are mispriced.
    Severity: Medium if broken
    Repro: curl -s -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer alice-token' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"items":[{"product_id":1,"quantity":1}],"coupon":"FREE100"}' http://127.0.0.1:8000/orders

tests.name: test_invalid_ids_and_tokens
tests.doc:
What: non-numeric order id -> 422, unknown id -> 404, malformed/unknown bearer token -> 401.
    Why: consistent error handling avoids stack traces and makes authorization decisions predictable.
    Severity: Low if broken
    Repro: curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer not-a-token' http://127.0.0.1:8000/orders/1

exchanges.body: {"detail":[{"type":"int_parsing","loc":["path","order_id"],"msg":"Input should be a valid integer, unable to parse string as an integer","input":"abc"}]}

tests.name: test_successful_login_returns_token
tests.doc:
What: POST /login with alice's correct password returns a bearer token that works on /users/me.
    Why: positive control for the lockout test, so lockout is not "passing" because login is simply broken.
    Severity: High if broken
    Repro: curl -s -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"username":"alice","password":"alice-pass-1"}' http://127.0.0.1:8000/login

tests.name: test_permission_matrix[anonymous-GET-/products]
tests.doc:
What: one cell of the role x endpoint permission matrix (tests/permission_matrix.py).
    Why: broken access control is the #1 API risk (OWASP API1/API5 2023); each cell in tests/permission_matrix.py (22 role/endpoint/method pairs taken from the spec's access rules) is checked, including negative cases.

tests.name: test_bola_user_cannot_read_other_users_order
tests.doc:
What: bob requests GET /orders/1, which belongs to alice.
    Why: object IDs are sequential, so any customer could read every order (names, items, totals) by counting upward.
    Severity: High
    Repro: curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer bob-token' http://127.0.0.1:8000/orders/1

tests.name: test_bfla_normal_user_cannot_list_all_users
tests.doc:
What: alice (role=user) calls the admin-only GET /admin/users.
    Why: the admin route only checks that a token is valid, not the role, so every customer gets the full user list.
    Severity: Critical
    Repro: curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer alice-token' http://127.0.0.1:8000/admin/users

tests.name: test_bfla_normal_user_cannot_create_products
tests.doc:
What: alice (role=user) calls the admin-only POST /admin/products.
    Why: write access to the catalog lets any customer add products at arbitrary prices.
    Severity: Critical
    Repro: curl -s -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer alice-token' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"name":"x","price":"0.01","stock":1}' http://127.0.0.1:8000/admin/products

tests.name: test_mass_assignment_cannot_set_role

finding.owasp: API3:2023 Broken Object Property Level Authorization (mass assignment)

tests.doc:
What: alice sends PATCH /users/me with {"role": "admin"}.
    Why: if the server copies every client field into the record, any user can promote themselves to admin.
    Severity: Critical
    Repro: curl -s -X PATCH -H 'Authorization: Bearer alice-token' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"role":"admin"}' http://127.0.0.1:8000/users/me

tests.name: test_sqli_union_in_product_search

finding.owasp: Injection - OWASP Top 10 A05:2025 (A03:2021), CWE-89; no dedicated API Top 10 2023 category (was API8:2019)

tests.doc:
What: GET /products?search= with a UNION SELECT payload that targets the users table.
    Why: the search string is pasted into SQL, so an anonymous caller can read any table (here: usernames and password hashes).
    Severity: Critical
    Repro: curl -s -G http://127.0.0.1:8000/products --data-urlencode "search=zzz' UNION SELECT id, username || ':' || password_hash, 0, 0 FROM users--"

tests.name: test_sqli_quote_in_search_is_handled

finding.owasp: Injection (A05:2025, CWE-89) + verbose DB error: API8:2023 Security Misconfiguration (CWE-209)

tests.doc:
What: GET /products?search=O'Reilly (a normal apostrophe).
    Why: a 500 with a raw database error on a quote is the classic sign of string-built SQL, and it leaks internals.
    Severity: Critical (same root cause as the UNION test)
    Repro: curl -s -G http://127.0.0.1:8000/products --data-urlencode "search=O'Reilly"

tests.name: test_profile_does_not_expose_password_hash

finding.owasp: API3:2023 Broken Object Property Level Authorization (excessive data exposure)

tests.doc:
What: GET /users/me as alice; the response must not contain credential fields.
    Why: password hashes in API responses end up in browser caches, logs and analytics, and can be cracked offline.
    Severity: Medium
    Repro: curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer alice-token' http://127.0.0.1:8000/users/me

tests.name: test_admin_user_list_does_not_expose_password_hash

finding.owasp: API3:2023 Broken Object Property Level Authorization (excessive data exposure)

tests.doc:
What: GET /admin/users as admin; even admins must not receive password hashes.
    Why: the admin UI never needs them; leaking them widens the blast radius of any admin-session compromise.
    Severity: Medium
    Repro: curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer admin-token' http://127.0.0.1:8000/admin/users

tests.name: test_order_total_with_coupon_matches_spec[3x-cable]

finding.owasp: Data accuracy (business logic) - pricing spec section 'Money'

tests.doc:
What: POST /orders with coupon SAVE10; compare total with the spec (10% off subtotal once, half-up).
    Why: wrong totals mean customers are over/under-charged on every discounted order, a direct revenue and compliance problem.
    Severity: High
    Repro: curl -s -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer alice-token' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"items":[{"product_id":1,"quantity":3}],"coupon":"SAVE10"}' http://127.0.0.1:8000/orders

tests.name: test_order_total_with_coupon_matches_spec[mixed-cart]

finding.owasp: Data accuracy (business logic) - pricing spec section 'Money'

tests.doc:
What: POST /orders with coupon SAVE10; compare total with the spec (10% off subtotal once, half-up).
    Why: wrong totals mean customers are over/under-charged on every discounted order, a direct revenue and compliance problem.
    Severity: High
    Repro: curl -s -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer alice-token' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"items":[{"product_id":1,"quantity":3}],"coupon":"SAVE10"}' http://127.0.0.1:8000/orders

tests.doc:
What: 10 wrong passwords for alice on POST /login; from the 6th attempt the API must answer 429.
    Why: without throttling an attacker can guess passwords at full speed (credential stuffing / brute force).
    Severity: Medium
    Repro: for i in $(seq 1 10); do curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} ' -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"username":"alice","password":"wrong'$i'"}' http://127.0.0.1:8000/login; done
